upper_bound.quote: **Proof.** This follows by a descent on the weight $w$ (standard; details omitted). $\square$
upper_bound.witness: The write-up must prove, for every $C\in\mathcal C$ and every $p\in C$, the existence of $D\in\mathcal C$ with $p\in D$ and $w(D\setminus\{p\})<a_1$. Merely naming a weight descent and explicitly omitting its details proves none of its cases.
upper_bound.load_bearing: This lemma is the sole reason every prime appearing in any minimal support must occur in one of finitely many terminal supports. Without it, the finite prime set $P$, finiteness of $\mathcal C$, and the resulting period are unsupported.

parsed.notes: Mapping: lower_bound is bounded-size finiteness via the infinite sunflower lemma and self-duality. Upper_bound is localization of every occurring prime into a bounded-size terminal minimal support via strict weight descent.
